title: Part-Time Shopify Web Designer / Developer
description:
Baie Botanique is a UK vegan skincare and mineral suncare brand. We are looking for a capable, reliable part-time Shopify Web Designer / Developer who can take a practical brief—such as “I want this section to look or behave like this”—and implement the solution without the founder having to work out the technical steps first.



This is a hands-on implementation and troubleshooting role. You should be comfortable working independently within an established Shopify store while keeping the brand presentation polished and consistent.



Responsibilities



• Build and edit Shopify pages and sections, including work in PageFly.

• Build or adapt custom Shopify sections and templates using Liquid, HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

• Plan and implement Shopify theme upgrades or migrations using a duplicate/staging theme. Preserve required apps, tracking, settings, content and custom functionality; test the new theme thoroughly; and maintain a safe rollback route before publication.

• Implement layout, styling and functionality changes using HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

• Fix spacing, alignment, typography, responsive-layout and mobile-display issues.

• Configure and troubleshoot Shopify apps, including upsells, sticky add-to-cart behaviour and related customer-experience features.

• Build and improve landing pages and product-page sections.

• Identify practical UX and conversion-rate improvements and implement approved changes.

• Take hands-on responsibility for diagnosing and fixing Shopify website-speed and performance issues—not simply producing an audit. Use tools such as Google PageSpeed Insights and Lighthouse to identify problems caused by themes, apps, scripts, images, fonts and page-builder content; implement approved fixes safely; and record measurable before-and-after results. Clearly escalate anything that genuinely requires an app provider or more specialised development.

• Test work carefully across desktop and mobile before marking it complete.

• Diagnose conflicts between themes, page builders, custom code and third-party apps.

• Keep a clear record of changes and explain what was changed, why and how it was tested.

• Follow tasks through to a verified result rather than stopping after the first attempted fix.



Examples of the work



Recent tasks have included PageFly edits, sticky add-to-cart behaviour, synchronising product variants between page elements, Selleasy upsell layout changes, mobile optimisation, CSS spacing and styling fixes, app configuration, promotional landing pages and general Shopify troubleshooting. Future projects may include moving the store to an updated theme and developing custom sections or functionality.



Essential experience



• Strong practical Shopify experience.

• Confident PageFly experience.

• Strong HTML and CSS, practical JavaScript, and working knowledge of Shopify Liquid and Online Store 2.0 theme architecture.

• Proven experience upgrading, migrating or substantially customising Shopify themes without disrupting live-store functionality.

• Experience configuring and resolving issues with Shopify apps.

• Proven hands-on experience fixing Shopify performance and page-speed issues, with an understanding of Core Web Vitals. You must be able to show changes you personally implemented and the measurable results.

• Good responsive-design judgement and attention to mobile usability.

• A good eye for polished e-commerce design, UX and conversion.

• Clear written English, careful testing and dependable follow-through.

• Ability to work from outcomes and briefs rather than requiring detailed technical instructions for every task.



Hours and pay



This is a part-time role with 5 guaranteed hours per week initially. Some weeks may require 10 or more hours when larger pages, launches or technical projects are underway. Additional hours will be agreed in advance.



Pay is US$7 per hour initially. Some weekday availability and overlap with UK working hours is required.



To apply, please answer the following:



1. Please share links to two or three Shopify stores or pages you personally built or substantially edited, and explain exactly what you did.

2. Describe your experience with PageFly, Shopify Liquid, HTML/CSS, JavaScript and Shopify app configuration. Include an example of a theme upgrade, migration or substantial theme customisation you personally completed, how you protected the live store, and what you tested before launch.

3. Give a specific example of a Shopify speed or performance problem you diagnosed and improved. What caused it, what did you change, which tools did you use, and what were the measurable before-and-after results?

4. If a sticky add-to-cart bar did not stay synchronised with the main product variant selector, how would you investigate the problem?

5. What hours are you available, what UK-hours overlap can you offer, and when could you start?



Shortlisted candidates may be invited to complete a short paid practical assessment.

title: Estimator
description:
Estimator



About Ultrabuild Construction Group



Ultrabuild Construction Group Pty Ltd is a growing Australian construction company delivering residential, commercial and government projects throughout Victoria, Australia. We are committed to quality workmanship, strong client relationships, and delivering projects safely, on time and within budget.

We're looking for an experienced Construction Estimator to join our team and take ownership of pricing and quoting across a mix of commercial, industrial, and residential projects. While we work across all three sectors, our current pipeline leans heavily toward structural steel work, so candidates with strong steel estimating experience will be prioritised.

This position will see you working closely with our project and construction management team on a day-to-day basis, so clear communication and reliability are essential.



Key Responsibilities



• Prepare accurate, detailed estimates and quotes for commercial, industrial, and residential construction projects

• Take off quantities and price structural steel packages (fabrication, supply, and/or erection scopes)

• Review architectural, structural, and engineering drawings to identify scope, materials, and labour requirements

• Source and compare supplier and subcontractor pricing

• Build and maintain priced assemblies, price lists, and estimating templates within Wunderbuild

• Manage quote requests to suppliers and subcontractors, and follow up on responses

• Assist in preparing client-facing proposals and quotes

• Flag risks, scope gaps, or pricing discrepancies before quotes go out

• Maintain organised, up-to-date records of all estimates and supporting documentation



Requirements



• Minimum 3–5 years' experience as a construction estimator

• Demonstrated experience estimating structural steel (essential)

• Solid understanding of commercial, industrial, and/or residential construction methods and documentation

• Hands-on experience using Wunderbuild (preferred, not essential)

• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy under deadline pressure

• Excellent written and verbal English communication skills

• Reliable internet connection and a suitable home office setup



Nice to Have



• Experience working with Australian builders, contractors, or construction companies

• Familiarity with Australian construction standards, terminology, and documentation conventions

• Experience with take-off software



What We Offer



• Competitive salary based on experience

• Long-term, stable remote position

• Opportunity to work directly with an Australian construction business

• Supportive team environment



How to Apply



Please submit your resume along with a short summary of your structural steel estimating experience.

Applicants with prior experience on Australian construction projects are encouraged to highlight this in their application, along with the words Coleraine Road.

title: Client Video Production Coordinator (Philippines Only)
description:
You may apply using this link::



About Us



Ylopo, LLC is a rapidly growing marketing and technology company providing internet marketing services and proprietary lead generation and engagement software to successful real estate agents across the country. We are seeking an outgoing, tech savvy individual to join our growing team.



 



Why work for Ylopo?



At Ylopo we offer team members:



a commitment to personal development,



guidance and support at a high level through interfacing with our Executive Team to prioritize goals as a company,



excellent leadership and mentoring for our entry-level to senior staff, and recognition of outstanding efforts,



team building events, team lunches/ happy hours, and other company wide events



a supportive, caring environment dedicated to continuous learning and growth.



The Digital Twin Studio Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the end-to-end process of creating digital twin videos for Ylopo clients using HeyGen's Digital Twin Studio. This role serves as the operational link between clients and the Digital Twin Studio production process—from collecting and validating the client's original video and consent to generating digital twin videos, testing scripts, and performing initial quality control. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, comfortable working with technology and video-based tools, and has a strong visual eye for identifying what looks natural, professional, and on-brand. The role requires someone who can confidently follow up with clients, troubleshoot basic issues, and maintain a high standard of quality throughout the digital twin creation process. 



 



Job Responsibilities



       1. Client Video Collection & Coordination



Coordinate with Ylopo clients to collect the original video recording required to create their digital twin.

Clearly communicate video recording requirements, specifications, and submission instructions to clients. 

Review submitted videos to ensure they meet the required technical and quality standards before processing. 

Identify missing or inadequate submissions and communicate specific requirements for resubmission. 

Follow up with clients via email or text to keep video submissions moving forward and prevent delays. 

 



      2. Consent & Documentation 



Ensure clients complete the required consent form/link authorizing Ylopo to utilize their submitted video for digital twin creation. 

Monitor outstanding consent requirements and follow up with clients as needed. 

Maintain accurate records of video submissions, consent completion, status, and outstanding client requirements. 

Ensure videos are not processed until the appropriate consent requirements have been completed. 

 



      3. Digital Twin Production 



Upload and process approved client videos using HeyGen Digital Twin Studio. 

Generate digital twin videos using different available looks, settings, and configurations. 

Run test scripts to evaluate the digital twin's appearance, voice, delivery, and overall presentation. 

Make appropriate adjustments within the available Digital Twin Studio settings to improve output quality. 

Become highly familiar with the Digital Twin Studio workflow and continuously improve efficiency and output quality.

 



     4. Quality Control & Attention to Detail 



Review generated videos carefully for visual and presentation quality. 

Develop a strong eye for what looks natural, professional, and appropriate for Ylopo clients. 

Identify issues such as unnatural movements, facial expressions, lip synchronization, visual inconsistencies, awkward delivery, or other quality concerns. 

Conduct basic quality control before videos move forward in the production process.

title: Design Manager — Canadian Property Developer, Remote
description:
We are a property developer in Nova Scotia, Canada. We design, build small and midsize buildings like condo / apartments.  



The problem, in plain terms. Our design process has no manager. Drawings go out without a revision mark, so a supplier prices the wrong set and a trade builds from the fourth version. Permit submissions come back with comments an internal check would have caught. Engineers, the municipality and suppliers find gaps in a package before we do. Changes get made on an old base. Decisions live only inside drawings, so six versions in, nobody can say why the building looks the way it does. Questions from our architects and our consultants sit unanswered because nobody owns the log. Our founder and chief of staff have carried this between them. It has cost us in rework, in permit time and in people. We are hiring the person who has run this properly before and will install it here.



WHAT YOU OWN



1. Drawing issue and revision control. A drawing register, revision marks and clouds, issue status, superseded-set control and a transmittal log, so at any moment we know which set is current and who holds it.



2. Stage gates with checklists. Concept approval, design development, permit submission, stamp readiness, issue for construction. Each has a checklist, a review and a sign-off, and nothing passes without them.



3. Design QA and coordination review. Completeness and clash checks across architectural, structural, civil, mechanical and electrical, schedules and shop drawings, before anything leaves us.



4. Consultant and engineering coordination. Scope and brief each engineer and consultant, hold an information-required schedule and an RFI log, run comment rounds, track stamps and sign-offs.



5. Authority approvals. Submission packages, a comment-response log, conditions tracking and resubmission control, across several municipalities.



6. Design change control. Every change after issue, from the owner, from site or from an engineer, is logged, impact-assessed, approved and re-issued under revision. Including ours.



7. The design brief and the standards library. Unit and room templates, site constraints and the cost target, confirmed complete before drawing starts, with our planning and pre-construction leads.



8. Design programme and resource planning. Deliverables per project against permit and construction dates, ETAs, weekly allocation and check windows for the design team.



9. Cost and buildability at every gate. Pre-construction and construction in the room when a concept is approved, so cost is a design input, not a discovery.



10. Construction-phase design support. A site query and RFI log, as-built deviations handled, red-marked sets and revised stamped plans issued under control, inside an agreed answer window.



11. The design team and its standards. Weekly allocation, reviews, feedback given privately, mentoring; title blocks, sheet numbering, naming, LOD definitions and model standards.



12. The project design record. Decision register, review minutes and actions, drawing register, RFI and approvals logs, in one place per project.



WHO YOU COORDINATE



In-house architects, and outside structural, civil, mechanical and electrical engineers, surveyors, geotechnical and architectural consultants. The mix changes per project. You run whichever mix a project has.



HOW HANDS-ON



This is a small team, so you produce some of it: concept sketches, redlines, templates and sheet setup, checking. What that cannot do is displace the management. When a production task and a coordination task collide in a week, coordination wins, and you plan the week so they rarely collide.



TECHNOLOGY



We run the company on software we write ourselves and we are adding AI throughout how we design, coordinate and record. You do not need to be a programmer. You do need to be the person who picks up a new tool in a week, is already using AI in design or coordination work, and can say what it changed and where it was wrong. Someone who waits to be trained will not keep up here, and we say that plainly because it matters more than most items on this page.



WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE AFTER TWELVE MONTHS



- Every set that leaves us carries a revision, and every recipient is in the transmittal log.

- Every project passes each gate with a checklist signed before the next stage starts.

- No completeness gap is found first by an engineer, a supplier or a municipality.

- Every change after issue is in the change log with its impact before it is drawn.

- Every project has a decision register that explains the building.

- Permit and handover dates are met.

- Questions from the design team and consultants are answered within one business day, or logged as an assumption they can proceed on.



WHAT WE NEED YOU TO HAVE DONE



- At least five years in design management, design coordination, or document and BIM coordination at a developer, general contractor, design-build firm or multi-disciplinary consultancy, on residential or similar buildings.

- You have personally kept a drawing register and a transmittal log, run gate checklists, run consultant comment rounds to stamp, and run municipal comment rounds to approval. You can describe each in your own words in an interview.

- You have run change control with impact assessment on live projects.

- You have held a line with people who did not report to you, sending work back and holding dates, and given hard feedback privately to people who did.

- An architecture, architectural technology or engineering background. Revit literacy: you read and check models and set up sheet and model standards.

- Already using AI tools in your work, and fast at adopting new ones.

- Remote-experienced, with a working overlap into the Atlantic Canada business day.



Useful, not required: Canadian codes (NBC Part 9) or municipal processes; having sat on the developer side of a brief; multi-unit wood-frame.



NOT A FIT



Revisions kept in the file name. "The engineer handles that." A permit comment log you cannot describe. Management described as assigning tasks and chasing status. A studio background with no consultants or authorities in it. Waiting to be trained on tools. If you build parametric tools rather than run design processes, see our Computational Designer posting.



HOW TO APPLY



Start your reply with the word DATUM. Applications without it are not read.



Answer these four. Short is fine. Specific is essential.



1. Your drawing control system on your last project: how sets were numbered and issued, how a revision was marked, how you knew who held which set, and what the log looked like.



2. A submission that came back with municipal comments, or a stamp that was withheld. How you ran it to approval: who did what, how you tracked it, and what you changed so it did not recur.



3. A change that arrived after issue, from the owner, from site or from an engineer. Where it was logged, who assessed the impact, who approved it, how it was re-issued.



4. One thing you changed in how you work in the last year because of a new tool, AI or otherwise. What it replaced, and one thing it got wrong.



OUR PROCESS, AND HOW FAST



We read replies the same day. Shortlisted candidates get a paid work sample on a real project of ours, about half a day, paid whether or not we proceed. Then one call with our founder. Then an offer. We aim to make an offer within a week of your application.

title: Quantity Surveyor – Residential Construction
description:
Remote | Full-Time

NZ-based Construction Company

We are a growing NZ-based residential construction company looking to add an experienced Quantity Surveyor / Estimator to our team. We are particularly looking for someone with genuine NZ and/or Australian residential construction experience, who is highly organised, communicates clearly and often, and can be trusted to own their work. If you hit a snag or aren't sure about something, we want to hear about it early — not find out further down the track when it's too late to fix.

If you take pride in accuracy, enjoy detailed estimating work, and want to be part of a business that values good systems, clear processes, and people who speak up, this role will suit you well.





About the Role

You’ll be responsible for pricing residential projects end-to-end, working closely with our NZ-based team to support upcoming work, and helping keep project cost tracking and admin on top of things once tenders are won. 



Key Responsibilities

Pricing & Tendering

Pricing residential tenders from concept through to submission

Reviewing architectural drawings, specifications, and consultant documentation

Requesting, tracking, and reviewing supplier and subcontractor quotes

Preparing detailed estimating sheets, tender summaries, and cost breakdowns

Identifying cost risks, gaps, and opportunities early in the pricing process

Ensuring tender documentation is accurate, consistent, and well organised

Project & Cost Support

Preparing and tracking progress claims against contract value as projects proceed

Maintaining and updating our supplier/subcontractor pricing list

Supporting project cost administration in Xero/Procore (loading projects, checking invoices against quotes)

Helping collect supporting documentation from consultants and subcontractors where needed

Communication

Providing regular, proactive progress updates on workload and tender timelines

Raising issues, blockers, or uncertainties as soon as they come up — we'd much rather hear "I'm stuck on this" early than find out later.









Who We’re Looking For

You’ll naturally align with a structured, detail-driven way of working:

Detail-focused and accurate – you don’t miss things





Highly organised – you work methodically and meet deadlines





Comfortable working remotely – disciplined, reliable, and self-managed





Process driven – and can meet targets and work schedules consistently.





Accountability – You take responsibility not only for the task but more importantly the outcome. Take ownership of your pricing outputs. 





Proactive communicator - You can proactively communicate with all team members in order to understand conditions and situations and you report proactively to team members and management where required.





Skills & Experience We Value

3+ years’ experience as a Quantity Surveyor or Estimator





Residential construction experience is essential





Genuine experience working with NZ and/or Australian construction companies





Strong ability to read and interpret architectural and engineering plans





Solid understanding of residential build processes, materials, and labour rates





Experience sourcing and analysing supplier and subcontractor pricing



Some exposure to progress claims and project cost tracking (Xero, Procore, or similar) is a plus





Proficient in Microsoft Office, Google Sheets, and digital estimating tools





Strong written and verbal English communication skills





High level of accuracy and attention to detail





Why Join Us

We are focused on doing residential construction properly — with good systems, clear communication, tidy sites, and quality outcomes. You’ll be working with an organised, professional team that values structure, consistency, and pride in workmanship. We work hard, support each other, and maintain a positive team culture along the way.



How to Apply

Please submit your CV and cover letter.

 subject line:

Greater QS – I’m the one you are looking for.

And in your cover letter, please include:

A brief summary of your NZ or Australian residential construction experience

title: Paralegal / Legal Assistant — California Corporate & Cannabis Licensing Filings
description:
Job Type: Full-Time (40 hours/week)

Salary: $1,000 – $1,600 USD/month (based on experience)

Work Setup: Permanent work-from-home, long-term

---

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are a California-based multi-location cannabis retail and cultivation company. We operate roughly 30 legal entities and hold state and local licenses across nine cities and counties. Every one of those entities and licenses has filing deadlines, renewal windows, and paperwork requirements attached to it.

We are looking for one detail-obsessed person to own that paperwork end to end.

This is not a general VA role. You will spend your days inside government filing portals, preparing and submitting corporate and licensing documents, and making sure nothing expires, lapses, or gets rejected. If you find deadline calendars and document checklists satisfying rather than tedious, you will do well here.



Important: This role does not involve giving legal advice or practicing law. You will prepare, organize, and submit filings under the direction of our COO and outside counsel. All filings are reviewed and signed by authorized U.S. signatories.

---

WHAT YOU WILL DO

California Secretary of State Filings (bizfileOnline)

Prepare and file Statements of Information for LLCs and corporations across ~30 entities

File Articles of Organization / Incorporation, amendments, and dissolution or cancellation documents

Process registered agent changes and foreign qualification filings

Order certified copies and Certificates of Status

Monitor entity status and flag anything that falls out of good standing

California Department of Cannabis Control (DCC) Licensing

Prepare and submit annual license renewal applications ahead of every deadline

Assemble new license applications and license modification requests

Maintain owner and financial interest holder disclosures as ownership changes

Upload and organize supporting documentation: premises diagrams, seller's permits, bonds, labor peace agreements, property owner consent forms, and local authorizations

Track and respond to deficiency notices with the correct supporting documents

Keep a master license register: license numbers, entity, expiration dates, and current status

Local Jurisdiction Permits

Track and renew city and county cannabis business permits, conditional use permits, and business tax certificates across multiple jurisdictions

Monitor local renewal calendars and prepare submission packets

Records and Calendar Management

Own a master filing calendar covering every entity and every license, with advance reminders built in

Maintain organized entity records in Google Drive: formation documents, operating agreements, EIN letters, resolutions, and licenses

Draft routine corporate resolutions and consents from existing templates for attorney review

Coordinate notarization, apostilles, and courier or mail submissions with our U.S. team

Track all matters and deadlines in Asana

---

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

REQUIRED

2+ years of paralegal, legal assistant, or corporate compliance work supporting U.S.-based clients

Direct hands-on experience filing with a U.S. Secretary of State or a comparable government portal

Excellent written English — you will draft correspondence and respond to government agencies

Genuinely exceptional attention to detail. In this role a wrong entity name or a missed date costs real money

Strong organizational systems: you build the tracker before you need it

Comfortable working independently and flagging problems early rather than sitting on them

Comfortable working in the cannabis industry (fully legal and regulated in California)

Reliable high-speed internet, a backup connection, and a quiet dedicated workspace

Able to sign an NDA and handle confidential owner information with discretion



NICE TO HAVE

Experience with California DCC, or cannabis licensing in any U.S. state

Familiarity with CDTFA, EDD, or California FTB filings

Experience managing filings for a large portfolio of entities

Working knowledge of Asana, Adobe Acrobat, Google Workspace, and RingCentral

Paralegal certificate or law degree from a Philippine institution

---

WORK SETUP

40 hours per week, Monday through Friday

Core schedule is flexible, but we need at least 3 hours of daily overlap with Pacific Time business hours (roughly 11:00 PM to 2:00 AM OR  6:00 AM to 9:00 AM Manila time) for handoffs and calls. The rest of your hours can be worked during your normal day

Permanent remote position

We provide access to all systems, tools, and training on our specific filings

---

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

$1,000 – $1,600 USD per month depending on experience

Paid time off after 3 months

Annual performance review with raise consideration

Long-term, stable position — we are hiring someone to grow with us, not for a short project

---

HOW TO APPLY

Please follow these steps exactly. Applications that skip a step will not be reviewed.

Put "SOS FILINGS — [Your Name]" in the subject line of your application.

In the body of your message, answer these three questions in your own words:

Describe a specific U.S. government filing you have prepared or submitted. What was it, what portal did you use, and what made it tricky?

How do you personally keep track of recurring deadlines across many different clients or entities? Describe your actual system.

What would you do if you discovered a filing deadline had already been missed?

Attach your resume.

Include a link to a sample of your written English — a work sample, a cover letter, or a document you drafted (redact any confidential information).

Create a short video (< 2 minutes) introducing yourself and explaining your experience.

We review every application that follows these instructions. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to complete a short paid test task before any interview.

title: Architect, AI Design  — Residential Developer (Canada)
description:
We are a property developer in Canada. We design, build and hold apartment buildings.  We run the company on software we write ourselves. 



This seat is the future of our architecture department. 



Here is what we mean. Today a concept is produced the way it has been produced for forty years: a site arrives, someone opens a model, and weeks later there is a set of options that nobody can fully explain. We want the person who looks at that and asks a different question: not how do I produce this one, but how do the next twenty get produced, correctly, in hours, with the checks built in. You will produce concepts yourself from day one with the best current tools, because the projects do not wait. And you will turn that production into a system, with our software lead, so that each project makes the next one faster and safer.



We are asking for a rare combination and we know it: real architectural depth, fluency in the current generation of design and feasibility tools and the judgment to evaluate them, and enough technical literacy to build yourself, or with an engineer, rather than hand them a wish list. If you have two of the three and are honest about the third, read on. If you have one, this is not the seat.



WHAT YOU OWN



1. The design logic. What makes a unit work, what makes a plan buildable, what a developer needs to see to d
. Encoded, not remembered.



2. Concept production. Site to option set: massing, unit mix, floor area, parking, yield, and whether each option clears spatial separation and egress. Delivered on dates, with the best tools available today, from your first week.



3. The kit. Our unit types, room standards, families and templates, so every concept starts from a library rather than a blank model.



4. The constraints. Zoning envelopes, setbacks, height, parking, limiting distance and unprotected openings, encoded from authoritative sources and tested against projects we have already built.



5. The generation system, with our software lead. Intake, generation, numbers, checks, output, driven by our AI agents. You bring the domain and the design logic; he brings the platform.



6. The checks. Rule checks that run on a model before anything is issued, so a municipality, an engineer or a supplier never finds a gap before we do.



7. The learning loop. Municipal comments, engineer comments, site deviations and cost actuals feed back into the kit, the constraints and the checks, every project.



8. Tool evaluation. You know the current platforms, what each is good for, where each breaks, and when to build instead of buy. You make those calls with evidence and you revisit them as the tools change.



WHAT YOU DO NOT OWN



Design direction. What the building should be is d
 at a gate by our founder against options and criteria. Your job is to make that decision easy and well informed.



Process control. Drawing control, gates, approvals, consultants and change control belong to our design manager, who gates your work the same way they gate an outside firm.



HOW THIS SEAT IS MEASURED



Two numbers, from month one. Concepts shipped on their dates. And hours per concept, falling every quarter. The first stops the system from swallowing the work. The second stops the work from swallowing the system.



WHERE IT GOES



The seat grows with what it builds: the feasibility product for partners, the design technology function, and if it goes as we intend, the head of design over both production and process. We hire people who have done the job and then widen the job.



WHAT WE NEED YOU TO HAVE DONE



- An architecture degree and at least meaningful experience in practice, including residential design development taken through permit. You can design a unit that works and you can tell when one does not.

- Used at least two of the current site-planning and feasibility platforms on real projects, for example TestFit, Forma, Giraffe, Archistar, Higharc, Hypar, Skema, Finch, Deepblocks, or built the equivalent in Grasshopper or Dynamo, and you can say precisely what each gets right and where it breaks.

- Built or led a design-automation workflow that other people used after you built it: a Grasshopper or Dynamo definition, a Revit API or pyRevit tool, a Python pipeline. Something that ran in production, not a personal experiment.

- Used a large language model or an agent inside a real design or feasibility workflow, not a chat window: tool calling, structured outputs, an MCP server, an agentic coding tool. You can say what it got wrong and how you constrained it.

- Read and applied a building code's spatial separation and egress provisions on a real project. The Canadian code is useful, not required; you will learn ours with our design manager and our consulting architect.

- Produced a concept or feasibility package inside a week that a developer d
 on.

- Remote-experienced, with a working overlap into the Canada business day, and able to explain what a tool does and cannot do to an owner who is not technical.



Useful, not required: production software engineering; Canadian zoning or NBC Part 9; Speckle, IFC or open BIM tooling; having worked inside a developer rather than a practice.



NOT A FIT



A portfolio of renders. A computational designer who cannot design a unit. An architect who has never automated anything. A software engineer without the architecture. Anyone who describes a platform by its marketing page rather than by where it broke on their project.



HOW TO APPLY



Start your reply with the word ENVELOPE. Applications without it are not read.



Answer these five. Short is fine. Specific is essential. Vague answers are the fastest way out.



1. Compare two of the platforms you have actually used, for a four-unit wood-frame townhouse on a narrow infill lot. What does each get right, where does each break, and what would you not trust either for?



2. That lot has limiting-distance limits on both side walls. What is the first calculation you run, what does it constrain, and how would you encode it so a system applies it correctly to the next lot?



3. You have produced one concept the conventional way. Describe, concretely, how you would make producing the next twenty a system: inputs, steps, what you automate first, what stays human, where the checks live, and how it fails safely.



4. Something you built or ran that used a language model or an agent in a real workflow. What did it call, what did it get wrong, and how did you constrain it?



5. A concept or feasibility you produced in under a week that went to a developer's decision. What was in the package, what was d
, and what did you get wrong?

title: Land Comps Specialist (Vacant Land Pricing Analyst)
description:
Peakridge Property Group is a U.S.-based land investment company that buys and sells vacant land across multiple states. Our business is built on disciplined pricing, accurate research, and fast execution. Every purchase decision we make is based on real data, not assumptions.



We are currently looking for a Land Comps Specialist (Vacant Land Pricing Analyst) to support our acquisitions process. This role is responsible for researching vacant land properties, analyzing comparable sales, and helping determine realistic offer prices based on actual market conditions.



This is not a sales role. It is a research and analysis role. You will spend most of your time reviewing data, pulling comps, working in spreadsheets, and documenting pricing logic clearly so decisions can be made quickly and confidently.



This position is best suited for someone who enjoys detailed research, working with numbers, and following structured systems.



What you’ll be responsible for:



Reviewing vacant land parcels that our team is evaluating for purchase



Researching recent comparable land sales in the same county or nearby areas



Analyzing acreage, access, location, pricing trends, and market activity



Calculating price-per-acre and identifying conservative value ranges



Flagging potential risks or inconsistencies in data



Recording comps, notes, and pricing logic clearly in spreadsheets or CRM



Supporting the acquisitions team with accurate, well-documented pricing analysis



What we are looking for:



Previous experience with real estate research, land comps, or property analysis



Strong attention to detail and ability to work consistently



Comfortable using spreadsheets and online research tools



Ability to follow pricing rules and avoid speculation or emotional valuation



Reliable computer and internet connection



Familiarity with land platforms such as LandPortal is a big plus, but not required



Why you’ll like this role:



Clear expectations and structured workflows



No cold calling, no selling, and no customer service work



Focused research tasks with minimal distractions



Long-term opportunity with a growing U.S.-based company



Performance-based bonuses tied directly to closed deals



Opportunity to grow into a more senior pricing or analytical role over time



Compensation:



$4 per hour



$100 bonus for every deal that successfully closes



SKILLS TEST (REQUIRED TO APPLY)



Please complete all of the following tests. Applications without completed tests will not be reviewed.



Test 1 – Pricing & Logic

In your own words, explain how you would determine a fair offer price for a vacant land property. Include what data points you would look for and how you would use comparable sales to arrive at a number.



Test 2 – Writing & Clarity

Rewrite the sentence below so it is clear, professional, and easy to understand:

“I look land price and maybe good but need check more to see if buyer want it.”



Test 3 – Research Ability

Using Google, find the county assessor or property appraiser website for Gila County, Arizona.

Paste the link and briefly explain what information on that site would be useful when pricing vacant land.



Test 4 – Attention to Detail

Lot A: 2.1 acres sold for $29,400



Lot B: 3.4 acres sold for $44,200



Calculate the approximate price per acre for each lot and explain which one would be more relevant when pricing a 2.5-acre parcel, and why.



HOW TO APPLY



Please submit:



Your resume



Your completed skills test answers



Include “Land Comps VA 2026” in the subject line of your application so we know you read the entire description.

title: Freight Broker Operations Support Specialist – U.S. Trucking & Logistics
description:
Modern Transit is looking for an experienced, highly organized Freight Broker Operations Support Specialist to join our growing U.S. transportation team.



This position will work directly with our freight brokerage operations team to help manage shipments from pickup through delivery. We are looking for someone who understands that great logistics operations require communication, urgency, accuracy, and follow-through.



This is more than a traditional virtual assistant position. You will become part of the daily operation of Modern Transit and help ensure our customers, carriers, and internal team receive excellent support.



What You'll Be Doing



• Conducting carrier check calls and monitoring shipments from pickup through delivery

• Communicating with drivers and carriers regarding shipment status, ETAs, delays, and exceptions

• Updating shipment statuses and notes within our Transportation Management System (TMS)

• Assisting with DAT load posting and carrier sourcing when needed

• Confirming pickup and delivery appointments

• Verifying that carriers are on-site for scheduled pickups and deliveries

• Providing proactive shipment updates to the Modern Transit operations team

• Identifying potential late pickups or deliveries before they become service failures

• Requesting and organizing PODs, BOLs, rate confirmations, and other shipment documents

• Assisting with detention, layovers, TONUs, and other shipment exceptions

• Building and updating loads within our systems

• Maintaining accurate records using Microsoft Excel / Google Sheets

• Supporting freight brokers and account managers with daily operational tasks

• Escalating urgent shipment issues to management when necessary

• Helping maintain organized, accurate, and professional communication throughout the shipment lifecycle



Who We're Looking For



Previous experience supporting a U.S.-based freight brokerage, trucking company, 3PL, dispatch operation, or logistics company is strongly preferred.



The ideal candidate has experience with some combination of DAT, TMS platforms, carrier communication, load tracking, freight brokerage operations, dispatching, Excel, Google Sheets, and U.S. trucking terminology.



We're especially interested in someone who can think instead of simply follow instructions.



If a driver hasn't moved in several hours, we want you to notice.



If an appointment is approaching and the truck isn't close enough, we want you to recognize the risk.



If a carrier stops responding, we want you to escalate the situation.



If something doesn't look right in the TMS, we want you to ask questions.



What Success Looks Like



A successful Operations Support Specialist helps our freight brokers spend less time chasing routine shipment information and more time serving customers, sourcing capacity, negotiating freight, and growing the business.



You'll be expected to communicate proactively, maintain accurate information, follow established processes, and take ownership of your responsibilities.



Skills We're Looking For



Strong written and spoken English is required. Candidates should also have excellent attention to detail, professional communication skills, good judgment, time management, computer proficiency, and the ability to work with multiple shipments and systems simultaneously.



Because you'll support U.S. transportation operations, candidates must also be comfortable working U.S. business hours.



Who We Are



Modern Transit is a growing transportation organization focused on providing dependable and responsive logistics solutions.



Our culture is built around faith, integrity, service, accountability, growth, and treating people the right way.



We're building a team for the long term. We're looking for people who want more than a temporary online job—we want individuals who are interested in developing their skills, taking on greater responsibility, and growing alongside Modern Transit.



How to Apply



Please include the following with your application:



A brief introduction about yourself.

The TMS platforms, load boards, or transportation software you've previously used.

Applications that do not include this phrase may not be considered.

title: Accounts Payable Clerk - Microsoft Business Central
description:
Position Summary

The Accounts Payable Clerk is responsible for the accurate and timely processing of vendor invoices, purchase order matching, vendor ledger maintenance, and payment runs within Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. This position ensures vendor accounts are reconciled, discrepancies are resolved promptly, and payments are issued accurately and on schedule.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, is comfortable working with purchase orders and vendor ledgers, and is detail-oriented, organized, and able to work independently in a fast-paced accounting environment.



Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Process incoming vendor invoices in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, matching invoices to purchase orders and receipts (2-way/3-way matching).

• Enter and code vendor invoices accurately, applying correct GL accounts, dimensions, and posting groups.

• Maintain accurate vendor ledgers; research and resolve discrepancies between vendor statements and Business Central ledger balances.

• Reconcile vendor statements to open accounts payable balances on a monthly basis.

• Prepare and process payment runs (checks, ACH, and wire transfers) in Business Central, ensuring payments are issued accurately and within vendor terms.

• Monitor the accounts payable aging report; flag past-due invoices and follow up with vendors or purchasing as needed.

• Set up and maintain vendor records, including W-9 collection and 1099 tracking.

• Respond to vendor inquiries regarding invoice and payment status in a professional and timely manner.

• Communicate with purchasing and warehouse teams to resolve purchase order discrepancies, including quantity and price variances.

• Use Continia Document Capture (or a comparable Business Central AP automation add-on) for invoice capture, approval workflow, and data entry, where applicable.

• Support month-end close activities, including accounts payable accruals and related general ledger account reconciliations.

• Assist with internal and external audit requests related to accounts payable.

• Maintain organized digital and physical accounts payable records in accordance with company policy.

• Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.



Required Qualifications

• 2+ years of accounts payable or general accounting clerical experience.

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central required, specifically within the accounts payable module (invoice entry, purchase order matching, vendor ledger entries, and payment processing).

• Experience with Continia Document Capture or a similar Business Central AP automation add-on strongly preferred.

• Solid understanding of the purchase order process and 2-way/3-way invoice matching.

• Demonstrated ability to reconcile vendor ledgers and vendor statements independently and resolve discrepancies.

• Experience preparing and processing payment runs (checks, ACH, wires) within an ERP system.

• Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills (lookups, filtering, basic reconciliation workbooks).

• High attention to detail and accuracy, with a demonstrated record of clean, well-documented work.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills to manage invoice volume and payment deadlines.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills for vendor and cross-department interactions.

title: Accounting Supervisor
description:
Role Purpose

The Finance & Accounting Supervisor is responsible for safeguarding the financial health of the organization by ensuring the accuracy of financial information, strengthening financial controls, managing cash flow and credit risk, supporting business decision-making, and developing a high-performing finance team.



The role exists to provide management with reliable financial information, improve financial performance, protect company assets, reduce financial risk, and ensure compliance with all statutory and company requirements.



This role is responsible for transforming financial data into actionable business insights, improving financial discipline across the organization, and ensuring the Finance Department contributes directly to business growth and operational excellence.



Core Outcomes (Primary KPIs)

The Finance & Accounting Supervisor will be evaluated on their ability to consistently deliver the following outcomes:



1. Financial Accuracy & Integrity

Ensure management can rely on accurate, complete, and timely financial information.

Success Indicators:

• Financial statements are accurate and submitted within established timelines.

• General ledger accounts are maintained accurately.

• Bank reconciliations are completed accurately and on time.

• Financial discrepancies are identified and resolved promptly.

• Audit findings and financial errors are are kept within established tolerances.



2. Cash Flow & Working Capital Management

Maintain visibility and control over the company's cash position.

Success Indicators:

• Cash flow forecasts are accurate and current.

• Cash flow risks are identified and communicated proactively.

• Liquidity requirements are effectively managed.

• Working capital performance improves over time.



3. Credit Control & Receivables Management

Improve collections and reduce exposure to bad debt.

Success Indicators:

• Overdue receivables are kept within established tolerances.

• Improvement in collection performance.

• Aging balances remain within acceptable targets.

• Credit risks are identified and escalated promptly.

• Collection strategies are implemented effectively.



4. Compliance & Financial Controls

Ensure the company remains compliant with statutory, regulatory, and internal requirements.

Success Indicators:

• VAT, PAYE, NIS, and other statutory obligations are submitted accurately and on time.

• Financial controls are maintained and strengthened.

• Internal control breaches are minimized.

• Financial records remain audit-ready.



5. Team Performance & Development

Build a capable, accountable, and continuously improving Finance team.

Success Indicators:

• Team members are coached and developed.

• Cross-training and knowledge sharing are implemented.

• Team productivity improves over time.

• Errors and rework are reduced.

• Department objectives are consistently achieved.



6. Process Improvement & Quality Management

Continuously improve financial processes, controls, and systems.

Success Indicators:

• Finance procedures are documented and maintained.

• Process inefficiencies are identified and improved.

• Corrective actions are completed effectively.

• Departmental compliance with QMS requirements is maintained.



Key Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & Analysis

• Prepare, review, and oversee the preparation of accurate financial reports.

• Ensure the integrity of financial records and accounting transactions.

• Analyze financial performance and identify trends, risks, and opportunities.

• Provide management with meaningful financial insights and recommendations.

• Support budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning activities.

• Monitor profitability, expenses, and overall financial performance.



Cash Flow Management

• Monitor cash balances and projected cash requirements.

• Assist management in maintaining healthy cash flow.

• Identify potential cash flow risks and recommend corrective action.

• Support management in financial planning and resource allocation.



Credit Control & Accounts Receivable Management

• Oversee accounts receivable and collections activities.

• Monitor customer credit exposure and aging balances.

• Develop and implement collection strategies.

• Support management in reviewing customer credit facilities.

• Escalate significant collection concerns and financial risks.

• Monitor and improve receivables performance metrics.



Accounts Payable & Financial Administration

• Oversee accounts payable processes.

• Ensure supplier obligations are managed appropriately.

• Verify financial transactions and supporting documentation.

• Ensure financial records remain complete and organized.

• Maintain fixed asset records and supporting documentation.



Payroll Support

• Collaborate with Human Resources to ensure payroll accuracy.

• Verify payroll information and related financial entries.

• Ensure payroll-related statutory obligations are accurately processed.



Financial Controls & Compliance

• Maintain strong internal financial controls.

• Ensure compliance with company policies and procedures.

• Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and statutory requirements.

• Support external audits and internal reviews.

• Investigate and resolve financial discrepancies.



Leadership Responsibilities

• Supervise and coordinate the activities of the Finance Department.

• Set clear expectations and accountability standards.

• Conduct regular coaching and development discussions.

• Identify training and development opportunities for team members.

• Build a culture of accuracy, accountability, professionalism, and continuous improvement.

• Conduct regular departmental meetings and performance reviews.

• Support succession planning and capability development within the department.



Quality Management System (QMS) Responsibilities

• Maintain assigned QMS documentation and records.

• Ensure Finance Department procedures remain current and effective.

• Participate in internal and external audits.

• Monitor corrective and preventive actions related to Finance/QMS activities.

• Identify opportunities for process improvement.

• Support continual improvement initiatives throughout the organization.

• Promote compliance with established quality standards and procedures.



Performance Expectations

The Finance & Accounting Supervisor is measured on outcomes, not activity.

Success is demonstrated through:

• Accurate financial reporting.

• Strong financial controls.

• Improved collections and receivables management.

• Effective cash flow management.

• Regulatory compliance.

• Reduced financial risk.

• Improved departmental performance.

• Continuous process improvement.

• Meaningful business insights that support management decision-making.

The role is expected to proactively identify risks, recommend solutions, and drive improvement rather than simply process transactions.



Qualifications

• Degree or Diploma in Accounting, Finance, ACCA, CPA, or related field.

• Minimum 3–5 years experience in Accounting or Finance.

• Previous supervisory or leadership experience preferred.

• Strong understanding of financial reporting principles.

• Working knowledge of Guyana tax, NIS, VAT, and statutory requirements.

• Experience with accounting software and financial reporting systems.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.



Core Competencies

• Financial Analysis & Business Acumen – Ability to interpret financial information and support sound business decisions.

• Financial Controls & Compliance – Strong understanding of controls, governance, and regulatory requirements.

• Leadership & Team Development – Ability to coach, develop, motivate, and hold team members accountable.

• Credit Control & Risk Management – Ability to manage receivables, identify risks, and improve collections.

• Planning & Organization – Ability to prioritize, coordinate, and manage multiple responsibilities effectively.

• Problem Solving & Decision Making – Ability to identify root causes and implement effective solutions.

• Communication & Influence – Ability to communicate financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial stakeholders.

• Process Improvement – Ability to identify inefficiencies and improve systems, controls, and workflows.

• Attention to Detail – Commitment to accuracy, quality, and completeness.

• Confidentiality & Professional Integrity – Maintains the highest standards of ethics, professionalism, and confidentiality.
